questions.question: What characterizes dynamic chemical equilibrium in a closed system?
choices: All particles stop moving
Reactant and product amounts must be equal
Only the forward reaction continues
Forward and reverse reaction rates are equal

questions.question: What is a reversible reaction?
choices: One that proceeds only until every reactant is gone
One that can proceed only toward products
One that cannot involve a reverse reaction
One that can proceed in both directions under suitable conditions

questions.question: What remains constant macroscopically at equilibrium under fixed conditions?
choices: The identity of individual reacting particles
Reactant and product concentrations
The direction of every collision
The number of forward reactions alone

questions.question: What does Le Châtelier's principle help predict?
choices: The exact time every reaction takes to finish
The atomic composition of an unknown compound
How an equilibrium responds to a change in conditions
The total energy used by an instrument

questions.question: For a fixed reaction, what change can alter its equilibrium constant?
choices: Changing temperature
Adding a catalyst at constant temperature
Changing initial concentrations at constant temperature
Changing vessel volume at constant temperature

questions.question: For A ⇌ B, an equilibrium mixture strongly favors B. Which description fits?
choices: The reverse reaction is impossible
The concentration of B exceeds that of A
The forward rate exceeds the reverse rate at equilibrium
Every molecule of A has necessarily disappeared

questions.question: Which system can maintain chemical equilibrium without material escaping?
choices: An open vessel continuously losing a gaseous product
A vessel continuously supplied with reactant and drained of product
A reaction mixture continuously separated into individual components
A closed reaction vessel

questions.question: Why does equilibrium not mean a reaction has stopped?
choices: Particles continue reacting in both directions
Only the forward reaction continues
Only the reverse reaction continues
Particle collisions no longer occur

questions.question: Why can reactant and product concentrations be unequal at equilibrium?
choices: Equilibrium requires equal masses instead
Only gases can reach equilibrium
Equal rates do not require equal concentrations
Products are not part of the equilibrium system

questions.question: What usually happens when a reactant is added to an equilibrium mixture?
choices: The equilibrium permanently disappears
All products must be removed
The system shifts toward consuming some added reactant
The reverse reaction becomes impossible

questions.question: What usually happens when a product is removed from an equilibrium mixture?
choices: The system shifts toward forming more product
All remaining reactants disappear instantly
The forward reaction must stop
The temperature must become zero

questions.question: What does adding a catalyst do to a system already at equilibrium?
choices: Shifts equilibrium entirely toward products
Changes the equilibrium constant at fixed temperature
Stops the reverse reaction
Speeds both directions without shifting equilibrium composition

questions.question: For an endothermic forward reaction, how does increased temperature usually shift equilibrium?
choices: Toward reactants
Toward products
No change because temperature never affects equilibrium
The equilibrium mixture must have equal concentrations

questions.question: For an exothermic forward reaction, how does increased temperature usually shift equilibrium?
choices: Toward reactants
Toward products
No change because temperature affects only rate
The equilibrium mixture must contain no products

questions.question: When pressure increases by reducing volume at fixed temperature, which gaseous side is favored?
choices: The side with more gas molecules in every case
The side with fewer gas molecules in the balanced equation
The side with heavier atoms in every case
The side with the catalyst

questions.question: For N2 + 3H2 ⇌ 2NH3, what does decreasing volume at fixed temperature favor?
choices: More N2 and H2
No change because both sides contain gas
Complete removal of all gases
More NH3

questions.question: For H2 + I2 ⇌ 2HI, all gaseous, what does decreasing volume at fixed temperature predict?
choices: A shift toward HI because it is a product
A shift toward H2 because it is lighter
No favored side from gas-molecule count alone
A shift toward whichever gas is darkest

questions.question: A sealed mixture has steady concentrations while molecules continue reacting both ways. What state is consistent with this?
choices: Dynamic equilibrium
A reaction that has completely stopped
A one-way reaction with constant reactant loss
An open system losing all products

questions.question: A catalyst is added to the same reversible reaction at the same temperature. Which comparison is expected?
choices: A different equilibrium constant is produced
Only reactants remain at equilibrium
The same equilibrium composition is reached faster
The reverse reaction no longer occurs

questions.question: Adding reactant changes the concentrations, but temperature stays fixed. What remains unchanged for that reaction?
choices: The initial reaction rate
The equilibrium constant
Every concentration during the adjustment
The total number of reactant molecules
